newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa's JSE launches enhanced trading system.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa's JSE launches enhanced trading system.

text.p: The Johannesburg Stock Exchange (JSE) on Monday implemented its feature-enhanced JET II trading system hitting few hitches after attempts last year to launch it were abandoned following major technical problems.
Leanne Parsons, general manager of markets at the JSE, said that the 29 new features of the electronic Johannesburg Equities Trading (JET) system had been put in place at the request of members.
"It is improving the functionality for the members," Parsons told Reuters.
"We implemented it this morning. We have spoken to the members and they are generally happy. Of course with any software there are one or two minor trouble spots," she said.
The JSE last November tried to implement JET II but nearly a week of breakdowns due to network problems saw the bourse revert back to JET I after major trade disruptions.

New JET II functions include a multiple entry system allowing dealers to enter up to 10 orders compared to only one on JET I. The size of a single order has been increased from 10 million rand to 25 million, Parsons said.
The reporting of corporate finance deals and assets swaps have been split as have that of foreign trades into sales and purchases.
Other features are improved price alerts, extra information on various price ratios and a faster ticker service on higher volumes.

Parsons said the next move on JET, which was first launched in March last year ending on-floor trade, would be to allow members to tap into it using their own systems. A "small release" of JET, to fix up some minor features, may be contemplated in the future, she said.
"But the intention is certainly not to enhance JET significantly, but to open it up so that members can have their own trading systems talking to JET."
Dealers on Monday expressed their satisfaction with JET II, noting its improved speed and greater transparency.

"The fact that we can enter a lot of deals at once makes it a lot quicker. As we can now see whether its a foreign purchase or sale and whether a corporate finance or asset swap deal means we don't have to guess anymore," one dealer said.
